scope_boundaries: Bounded mass and a fixed smooth big reference background remain chapter premises.
Uniform constants depend on fixed forms, strict analytic potential and a common positive lower-volume bound, not on the varying potential or intermediate background.
Gauge invariance concerns singularity volumes and the comparison after ordinary projection, not individual envelope mass.
The varying backgrounds dominate the reference and approach it from above; they need not be monotone.
Analytic approximants need not initially have a common positive lower-volume bound; a positive bound for corrected models is derived.
Capacity convergence is asserted for corrected ordinary models, not arbitrary analytic representatives.
Two-sided arbitrary background changes, zero-lower-volume analytic closure, triangle inequality and metric identification remain unestablished here.
